claims.claim: Recent Western nuclear builds have completed at costs in the mid-to-high teens of billions of dollars per gigawatt: Vogtle units 3-4 cost $36.8 billion for two ~1.1 GW AP1000 reactors (~$16-17bn/GW).
claims.episode_span: whose completed costs have run in the mid-to-high teens of billions of dollars per gigawatt
claims.supporting_quote: Construction cost Units 1–2: $8.87 billion (1989 USD) [ 1 ] ($19.5 billion in 2024 dollars [ 2 ] ) Units 3–4: $36.8 Billion

claims.claim: Licensing consumes years before construction: Vogtle's combined construction and operating license was applied for in March 2008 and approved by the NRC in February 2012 -- about four years -- consistent with the digest's four-to-ten-year range.
claims.episode_span: the extended licensing and permitting timeline, which can consume four to ten years before first concrete
claims.supporting_quote: In February 2012, the NRC approved the construction license of the two proposed AP1000 reactors at Vogtle

claims.claim: A gigawatt-scale reactor's bulk material inputs are tens of thousands of tonnes of steel and on the order of two hundred thousand cubic meters of concrete (a standard figure is under 40 t steel and 190 m3 concrete per MW).
claims.episode_span: Commodity steel might total on the order of twenty to thirty thousand tonnes
claims.source_title: Constructing a lot of nuclear power plants is not material constrained | NextBigFuture.com
claims.supporting_quote: Modern nuclear reactors need less than 40 metric tons of steel and 190 cubic meters of concrete per megawatt of average capacity

claims.claim: Financing cost on a nuclear build is interest on capital dictated by the construction period, and long construction periods have pushed up financing costs very significantly.
claims.episode_span: Carrying costs on capital compound at several percent per year across the full schedule
claims.source_title: Economics of Nuclear Power - World Nuclear Association
claims.supporting_quote: Financing cost is the interest charge on debt, dictated by the construction period and interest rate applicable. The construction time of a nuclear power plant is usually tak

claims.claim: Long construction periods have historically pushed up nuclear financing costs very significantly, supporting the digest's claim that multi-year delays compound the interest burden.
claims.episode_span: turning a five-year delay into an effective doubling of the interest burden
claims.source_title: Economics of Nuclear Power - World Nuclear Association
claims.supporting_quote: Long construction periods will push up financing costs, and in the past they have done so very significantly

claims.claim: The US NRC already has a design-certification pathway that approves a reactor design independent of any application to build or operate a specific plant (the 'certify once' mechanism the digest calls for).
claims.episode_span: the regulatory pathway would need to certify a design once and then apply that certification to subsequent identical units, shifting the review burden from each site to the manufacturing process itself
claims.source_title: Design Certification Applications for New Reactors | Nuclear Regulatory Commission
claims.supporting_quote: By issuing a design certification, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approves a nuclear power plant design, independent of an application to construct or operate a plant.

claims.claim: 'Modular' in SMRs means fabricating major nuclear-steam-supply components in a factory and shipping them to the site; even current large plants still need substantial field assembly.
claims.episode_span: Small modular reactors illustrate one attempt to attack these constraints by reducing module size to something that can travel by rail or barge and by designing for factory repetition from the outset.
claims.source_title: Benefits of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) | Department of Energy
claims.supporting_quote: The term “modular” in the context of SMRs refers to the ability to fabricate major components of the nuclear steam supply system in a factory environment and ship to the point of use. Even though current large nuclear power plants incorporate factory-fabricated components (or modules) into their designs, a substantial amount of field work is still required to assemble components into an operational power plant.

claims.claim: The NRC's Part 52 process (established 1989) bundles a construction permit and operating license into one combined license, and its certified standard plant designs serve as pre-approved designs.
claims.episode_span: Public and political reviews add further sequential steps that cannot be overlapped without new agreements.
claims.source_title: Backgrounder on Nuclear Power Plant Licensing Process | Nuclear Regulatory Commission
claims.supporting_quote: The NRC worked to improve regulatory efficiency and add greater predictability to the process by establishing an alternative licensing process, 10 CFR Part 52, in 1989. Part 52 includes a combined license that provides a construction permit and an operating license with conditions for plant operation.
